challenge.better_approach: In-house: commit_crossing_records (79875eb17ac2), 2955a4a316d3 (clearance refusal crossing), ee9637b02525 (sail verb crossing) commit the class-space records only; none commits the commons state. Grepped tickets for commons state commit by a crossing: none.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That every uncommitted crossing came through a verb (sail cross/verdict) rather than a close that failed midway: measured only for the three FIXME and one SUPERSEDED crossings I know; the 7cae18f7f9c2 BUILDME crossing's path is unread.
challenge.prior_art: Looked: a hook or the close script committing the commons after the fact (set aside: the dirt is exactly what a crossing without close.sh leaves, ticket 79875eb17ac2's own finding); having sail call commitcommons (set aside: sail would then reach a bin command, and Ticket.failed paths would still leave it).
challenge.real_collision: Possible with 12443bcc113f (another ticket's records do not refuse a crossing): committing own records at the verb is consistent with it; no Law contradicted. Distinction recorded.

answers.falsifier: after Ticket.passed or Ticket.failed on a ticket whose commons state file is tracked, git status --porcelain in the commons shows that state file clean, and a commit in the commons names it
answers.from_idea: none, because it is a measured gap: see cairn/machines/ticket/intention+why.json
answers.how: A hypothesis, not a settled shape: the public_interface is the class Ticket, so the commons commit belongs inside Ticket.passed and Ticket.failed beside the existing commit_crossing_records call, not a new public function. Either commit_crossing_records takes an optional commons_state path and commits it in the commons repo (a second path-limited git -C of the commons work tree), or a private sibling _commit_commons_state does and both run from the same call sites. Choose by the charter: a sibling stays private and needs no public_interface change. The commons commit stays path-limited (the ticket's state file and the artifact journal line it moved) and never stages another ticket's dirt. Depends on 79875eb17ac2, 2955a4a316d3 and ee9637b02525 landing first.
answers.traces_to: Law 7 (permanent in records of truth: a crossing that exists on one disk is not permanent); Law 4 (enforced by physics, not by a hand remembering sail step 10); Law 5 (the repo is itself the state of the machine).
answers.what: Ticket.passed, Ticket.failed and the sail crossing commit the ticket's commons state.json, path-limited, in the same act as the component's history.json and state.json.

bullets.text: Measured: 2026-11-19, read by cc_0 and confirmed by git show on origin: crossings 1648858dd (633a76c125d2) and 89447c4a6 (c408f2c1e66d), both DROPPED, committed only .artifact-journal.jsonl and cairn/devices/codemother/machines/clearance/{history,state}.json; the two tickets' commons state files stayed dirty until a hand commit, commons 0595ae5b3 ('633a76c125d2, c408f2c1e66d: DROPPED'). The ticket machine's published helper commit_crossing_records (ticket 79875eb17ac2, on its stacked branch, not yet landed) path-limits to the component's two files in the class-space repo only; the ticket's charter public_interface lists only Ticket and GATE_HOLDER.

title: Ticket.passed, Ticket.failed and the sail crossing commit the ticket's commons state.json, path-limited, in the same act
